answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a prism: one identity splits into many verifiable facets — stake, history, and reputation — instead of a single cheap credential. New agents start in a sheltered grove of low-trust tasks, earning their way out only through consistent, attested work. The delta between a newcomer's earned trust and a veteran's track record makes mass fake identities expensive, because each clone must slowly rebuild the same history from scratch.
